### Themes

Go to the following link to learn about different themes for RMarkdown!

<https://rpubs.com/ranydc/rmarkdown_themes>{.filelink}

### Add a table of contents

```{verbatim}
---
title: Lab
author: Your Name
output:
    html_document:
        toc: true
        toc_float:
            collapsed: true
---
```
![](/assets/toc.png)

### Print nicer dataframes and tables

To create tables with pages, use the following in your yaml.

```{verbatim}
---
title: Lab
author: Your Name
output:
    html_document:
        df_print: paged
---

```

![](/assets/paged_table.png)

To create nice tables *without* pages, use the following in your yaml.

```{verbatim}
---
title: Lab
author: Your Name
output:
    html_document:
        df_print: kable
---

```

![](/assets/kable_table.png)


### Tabsets

To create tabsets, use the following code:

````{verbatim}
## Title of page with tabs {.tabset}

### Title of tab 1

Some tab content

### Title of tab 2

```{r}
# Some code here
```
````

![](/assets/tabs.png)


### Remove unwanted warnings and messages

To remove unwanted warnings and messages from the output, use these at the very top of a code block. For instance, the following removes the warning messages from loading packages.

````{verbatim}
```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

data <- read_csv("heights.csv")

```
````

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

data <- read_csv("./data/heights.csv")

```


### Round values to fewer decimals

Use `round()` to round to fewer decimals. For example, the following rounds the variables `a` to two decimal places.

```r
round(a, 2)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

summary_table <- data %>% group_by(sex) %>% summarize(count=n(), Mean=mean(heights), SE = sd(heights)/count)

CIs <- summary_table %>% mutate(CIs = paste0("[", round(Mean-1.96*SE,2), ", ", round(Mean+1.96*SE,2), "]")) %>% select(sex, CIs)

```



### Create outputs like `r CIs[1,2]`

Use `paste0()` to add together strings and variables. This is useful for reporting CIs. For instance,

```r
CIs <- CIs %>% mutate(CIs = paste0("[", round(LowerCI,2), ", ", round(UpperCI,2), "]")) %>% select(group, CIs)
CIs
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| 
CIs
```

### Reference variables from r code directly in your paragraphs

Use ``` `r ` ``` to use r code in your paragraphs so you can reference variables from you code chunks. For example:

```{verbatim}
The the CIs for groups one and two are `r CIs[1,2]` and `r CIs[2,2]`, respectively.
```

The the CIs for groups one and two are `r CIs[1,2]` and `r CIs[2,2]`, respectively.

Note that [1,2] stands for row 1 and column 2 of the CI table, and [2,2] stands for row 2 and column 2 of the CI table.
